readiness_verdict.recommendation: Do not train 50M tokens on the existing 2.11M corpus alone (23.6 epochs). Execute Configuration A: expand unique corpus to 10.0M tokens using public-domain Project Gutenberg and open-access scientific literature before launching the 50M campaign.

configurations.name: Configuration A: Balanced Multi-Domain (Recommended)
configurations.rationale: Balances high lexical diversity, legal provenance, and optimal 5-epoch replay.
recommended_sources: Project Gutenberg Public Domain Classics (Melville, Swift, Defoe, Wells, Bronte - 4.5M tokens)
Open-Access Computing & Physics Papers (arXiv cs.DC, cs.AI, physics - 2.0M tokens)
Technical System Standards (IETF RFCs, Linux Kernel Documentation - 1.4M tokens)
configurations.operational_risk: Low. Minimal memorization risk with 5 epochs; high lexical diversity across technical and classical literature.

configurations.name: Configuration B: High-Diversity Open-Science
configurations.rationale: Prioritizes maximum out-of-distribution generalization with low epoch replay (3 epochs).
recommended_sources: Full Gutenberg Classical Literature Library (10.0M tokens)
Open Science & Mathematics Foundations (arXiv, Euler, Newton, Faraday, Maxwell - 4.5M tokens)
Open Source C/C++ System Code & Documentation (Linux, Git, SQLite - 2.2M tokens)
configurations.operational_risk: Very Low. 3 epochs avoids memorization; higher data preparation engineering effort.

configurations.name: Configuration C: Compute-Constrained Extended Replay
configurations.rationale: Conservative corpus expansion for rapid deployment with moderate replay (9 epochs).
recommended_sources: Targeted Public Domain Fiction (Melville, Hawthorne, Poe, Verne - 3.39M tokens)
configurations.operational_risk: Medium. 9 epochs on 5.5M corpus begins to exhibit early memorization on infrequent unigrams.
